en.question: A team's first instinct for every new feature is to build an autonomous agent. What is the most important counterargument?

options.text: Agency costs predictability, latency, and money, so add it only when needed.
Agents are considerably harder to implement in Python than workflows are.
options.note: Implementation effort is a real difference but not the core objection.

options.text: An agent cannot be given more than a handful of tools before it degrades.
options.note: Large tool sets do hurt selection accuracy, but no such hard limit exists.

options.text: Agents require dedicated long-running infrastructure that workflows avoid.
options.note: Deployment topology is unrelated to the choice of pattern.

en.explanation: The recommended posture is the simplest solution that works, with complexity added only when it demonstrably improves outcomes. Autonomy buys adaptability and pays in unpredictability, extra calls, and harder debugging.
